title: Attenuated shadow seeding with consensus rollback oracle
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces controlled shadow seeding mode and a multi-signal rollback oracle; opt-in via rollout policy. Improves safety when seeding new models into production traffic.
description:
Summary: Implements an 'attenuated shadow seeding' flow and a lightweight 'consensus rollback oracle' to make early-stage A/B and shadow experiments safer. This PR adds a policy-driven shadow sequencer that starts with heavily attenuated shadow traffic, monitors multiple telemetry signals, and escalates or withdraws seeding based on a consensus of metrics. Motivation: teams running shadow or A/B experiments saw accidental traffic spikes and lacked a clear automated rollback policy that accounts for correlated signals (latency, error rate, quality regressions). This change reduces blast radius for newly onboarded model variants and automates rollback decisions while preserving observability and operator control.

What changed (high level):
- New rollout policy type: "attenuated_shadow" that can be attached to model routes. Policy fields include initial_fraction, ramp_schedule, attenuation_strategy (fixed|exponential|adaptive), and consensus_threshold.
- Shadow Sequencer: runtime component that samples production requests and forwards copies to shadow variants at configured attenuation. Supports session/trace affinity options so shadowed requests keep correlated keys for meaningful telemetry.
- Consensus Rollback Oracle: evaluation agent that computes a weighted vote across signals: p50/p95 latency deltas, 5xx error delta, model-quality eval metric (if provided), and a user-defined smoke test gauge. If the consensus crosses the configured threshold for a sustained window, the oracle triggers a rollback escrow action.
- Rollback Escrow: instead of instant revert, we place the candidate into an escrow state that reserves traffic tokens and snapshot state (KV cache warmup token) and notifies operators with suggested actions (auto-backout, quarantine, or require manual approval). Escrow supports timed automatic unwind if operator does not act within hold_timeout.
- Observability: added per-policy dashboards (rollout_fraction, consensus_score, escrow_state) and tracing/span annotations so entire attenuation lifecycle is visible in the Console. Hooked into existing alerting rules and added a small set of smoke probes for early detection.
- Config/Policy UI: Console changes to create/preview attenuated shadow policies and a CLI flag to enable experiment dry-run mode.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Attenuation is enforced at the sequencer; we intentionally keep the runtime path for production requests unchanged to avoid impacting latency SLOs. Shadow copies are asynchronous and optionally hedged to avoid overloading model pools.
- Consensus instead of single-signal thresholds reduces false positives but requires careful weighting. Default weights are conservative (latency 30%, errors 35%, quality 30%, smoke 5%) and documented in the policy schema.
- Escrow provides a middle-ground: automatic containment without aggressive immediate removal, giving operators time to investigate while preventing full promotion/traffic commit.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for policy parsing, attenuation math, and consensus scoring (new test files added under runtime/rollout/). Total added unit tests: 48.
- Integration test harness that simulates a production lane with controlled latency and error injections. Verified that attenuation prevents >1% extra load on candidate pools at defaults.
- Canary on dedicated infra: staged deployment to canary DC with 10k qps replay for 4 hours. Observed no regression in p95 for primary route.
- Load tests to confirm shadow forwarding tail latencies are bounded and memory usage remains stable.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Rohit Varma: "This looks good overall. Two questions: 1) how do we guarantee the sequencer's attenuation doesn't drift under heavy load? 2) Are smoke probes mandatory for the oracle?"
- Maya Chen (author): "1) sequencer uses a token-bucket backed sampling window with counters persisted to the local node; added a compensating feedback loop to tighten sampling if we detect drift — see sequencer.go lines 160-200. 2) Smoke probes are optional in the policy, the oracle will still compute consensus without them but their presence increases sensitivity to functional regressions."
- Ethan Park: "Please add a short circuit to avoid forwarding if shadow pool capacity is below the min_capacity threshold — else we can overload smaller pools."
- Maya Chen: "Added min_capacity check and unit tests cover the behavior."
- Priya Nair: "We should ensure audit logging shows when escrow triggers and operator actions taken." 
- Maya Chen: "Audit logging emitted for escrow enter/exit as part of escrow_manager.go; added console UI button actions that produce audit entries."
- Rohit Varma: "Approve after small lint fixes and one more integration run against canary infra."
- CI: "All rollout pipeline checks passed after rerun (security scan, lint, unit, integration, e2e smoke)" 

CI summary: initial run had lint failure (console TS formatting). After fixes, rerun passed all checks: unit tests (48 new), integration harness, security scanner, and e2e smoke. ci/rollout-pipeline shows green on merge.

Migration and rollout plan:
- Ship behind feature flag: rollout.attenuated_shadow.enabled = false by default.
- Ramp console feature to internal teams for 1 week, then enable for self-serve.
- Create two sample policies in docs for common patterns: "controlled-seed-small-variant" and "fast-expunge-guarded".

Operational playbook (docs/runbooks/attenuated-shadow.md): contains steps for investigating consensus triggers, commands to move escrow -> quarantine -> rollback, and how to replay shadow traces for post-mortem.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main. Post-merge automation created a release note draft and a follow-up Linear ticket (ENG-2412) for telemetry weight tuning and UX polish.

Notes for maintainers: monitor consensus_score and escrow_state metrics closely for the first two weeks after enabling feature flag in production. Expect a handful of false positives; weights can be tuned per-team via policy overrides.
